findings.claim: The local replica migration cannot upgrade an existing non-empty revision-3 `cases` table because it adds multiple `NOT NULL` columns without defaults.
findings.evidence: `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` creates `cases` without `case_number`, `patient_id`, `surgeon_id`, `payer_id`, or `revision`, while `PGLITE_CASE_SUMMARY_SQL` later runs `ALTER TABLE cases ADD COLUMN case_number TEXT NOT NULL, ADD COLUMN patient_id UUID NOT NULL, ADD COLUMN surgeon_id UUID NOT NULL, ADD COLUMN payer_id UUID NOT NULL, ADD COLUMN revision BIGINT NOT NULL...`; PostgreSQL/PGlite rejects adding a non-null column with no default when existing rows are present. The added runtime plans in `replica-mounted-runtime.ts` and `replica-browser-memory.ts` require `migrateReplicaSchema(...).status` to be `ready` before constructing the projector/runtime, so a user with persisted pre-revision-6 case rows would fail startup rather than migrate.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the case-summary migration upgrade-safe: add columns nullable, backfill or rebuild from an authorized cold refetch, then enforce NOT NULL only after the table is empty/backfilled; alternatively detect this migration as requiring a controlled replica rebuild instead of expecting `ready`.
